post.description: Generates a TOTP secret (issuer `APILens`, account the user's email) and stores it encrypted and unconfirmed; returns the secret and its `otpauth://` URI for a QR code. Calling it again before `/2fa/verify` replaces the pending secret. Needs a sign-in less than 10 minutes old (`reauth_required` otherwise); answers `already_enabled` when 2FA is on.

Checks a code from the authenticator app against the pending secret (one 30-second period of skew either way). On success 2FA is on: returns ten single-use backup codes, shown this once. Audited as `totp.enabled`; a security alert is emailed. Answers `invalid_totp` for a wrong code, `invalid_request` when `/2fa/enable` was not called and `already_enabled` when 2FA is already on.

Public. Emails a 6-digit code and a magic link (15 minutes, single use) to the address. Always answers 200 `{sent: true, retry_after}` whether or not the address has an account; for `intent=signin` with no account the email offers sign-up instead. Within 30 seconds of the previous email for the same address and intent no new email is sent and `retry_after` is the remaining wait. Rate-limited per client IP and per email address (429 `rate_limited` with Retry-After).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; mirrors `retry_after`.

get.description: Public browser navigation. Starts an authorization-code flow with PKCE (and an OIDC nonce for Google), keeps the attempt server-side for 10 minutes keyed by a random state, and redirects (302) to the provider. Rate-limited per client IP. A provider that is not configured answers 404.
